 Moderator: 
Good afternoon, everyone and welcome to the UCO Bank Q2 FY27 Earnings call. 
Today from the management side, we have with us: 
o Mr. Rajendra Kumar Saboo – Managing Director & CEO (I/C) and 
Executive Director 
o Mr. Vijay N Kamble - Executive Director 
With this I hand over the call to MD sir for his opening remarks, post which we 
will have a Q&A session. Thank you and over to you, sir.  
 
- Mr. Rajendra Kumar Saboo - MD & CEO (I/C) and ED, UCO Bank: 
- Good afternoon to all, and welcome to all analysts and investors in this Analyst 
Meet Concall for the financial results of UCO Bank for the quarter ended 30th  
September, 2026. Already the results have already been published on the 
websites of the stock exchanges. This release has also been published, and the 
detailed presentation has also been placed on the websites of BSE and NSE, as 
well as on our bank's website. I hope that you must have gone through that. Still, 
I will give a brief of the various highlights of our results for the Quarter and Half 
Year ended 30th September, 2026.  
- The total business of the bank has reached to Rs.6,37,280 crore, registering a 
growth of 18.81% year-on-year. In this, the gross advances, the global advances 
of the bank, have grown by 24.70% year-on-year, reaching to Rs. 2,87,690 crore. 
And our total deposits have grown by 14.36%, reaching to Rs.3,49,590 crore for 
the period.  
- Out of this deposit, CASA growth has been 10.59% year-on-year, reaching to 
Rs.1,22,259 crore, in which savings deposits have grown to Rs.1,37,736 crore with 
a growth rate of 9.10%, and current deposits have grown to Rs.18,523 crore with 
a growth rate of 19.70% year-on-year. Thereby, our CASA ratio has been 
maintained at 36.77%. This is slightly lower than the June quarter.  
- Whereas, the advances have grown by 24.70%, the growth has come from all the 
sectors, like Retail, Agri, MSME and Corporate. So, the Retail advances have 
grown by 30.23%, and Agriculture has grown by 29.59%, and MSME has grown 
by 20.32%. And overall RAM sector growth has become 26.92%. And the total 
RAM portfolio stands at Rs.1,68,736 crore. 
- With this growth in advances and deposits, our profitability has also improved. 
So, our operating profit is Rs.1,872 crore for the quarter, with a growth of 16.04%. 
Net profit has grown to Rs.786 crore, a growth of 26.77% year-on-year, as against 

Page | 3  
 
Rs.620 crore in the last year, September 2025. The NIM has been maintained at 
3% for the global, and the domestic NIM has been maintained at 3.19% for the 
quarter. 
- This profitability is also coupled with asset quality improvement as well. So, our 
gross NPA ratio has reduced year-on-year by 60 basis points to 1.96%, and the 
net NPA ratio has improved by 25 basis points year-on-year. The net NPA ratio 
stands at 0.18% as on 30th September, 2026. 
- If you see these growth rates, profitability and NPA position, the actuals are 
exceeding the guidance which we gave at the beginning of the year, except for 
the CASA ratio. So, while we had given growth guidance in deposits of 10 to 
12%, our growth has been 14% plus. We had given guidance in advances growth 
of 12 to 14%; the growth has been 24.70%. Our guidance on the GNPA was to 
make it less than 2% by 31st March, 2027; we have already, in the half year, 
brought it down to below 2%, and our GNPA ratio is 1.96%. In the same way, 
our guidance for the net NPA ratio was to bring it down below 0.25% for the 
year, but in the half year itself we have brought it down to below 0.20%, that is 
0.18%. 
- Our capital adequacy ratio stands at 18.85%, with a Tier 1 ratio of 17.27%. Our 
CD ratio has improved to 82.29%, as against 75.47% in the previous year. Our 
total provision coverage ratio, including TWO has increased to 98.36%. 
- Then, our net interest income, if you go deeper into the profitability, has grown 
by 13.96% year-on-year to Rs. 2,886 crore. Our cost of funds has increased 
somewhat, a little bit, to 4.44%. Our yield on advances is 8.11% for the domestic 
and 7.79% for the global for the quarter. 
- Our cost-to-income ratio is 50.39% for the quarter ended 30th September 2026. 
Return on assets is annualised at 0.80%, which was 0.71% last year. And out of 
the non-interest income, our fee-based income has grown 34.66% to Rs.558 crore 
in the quarter. 
- On our slippage ratio we had also given guidance to keep it below 1%, and for 
the quarter it is 0.85%. So, thereby, we have also maintained our slippage ratio 
and our slippage ratio is also below the given guidance.  
- The productivity has also improved. Business per employee of the bank stands at 
Rs.30 crore, which was Rs.25 crore last year. In the same way, business per 
branch has also improved to Rs.185 crore, as against Rs.161 crore last year. We 
have a branch network of 3,439 branches, and we have added 27 branches. We 

Page | 4  
 
have three international branches, Hong Kong, Singapore, and we have opened 
our GIFT City IBU also in this quarter only.  
- So, mainly this is the highlight of the business, profitability and asset quality. I 
will quickly present a few initiatives we have taken during the last quarter, 
which have helped us in growing the business as well as improving profitability 
and asset quality.  
- As we all know, CBDC is also a very important development in the Indian 
economy, so our bank is also working to bring a CBDC offering to the customers. 
In the last quarter we have launched two special features on CBDC. One is the 
UCO Digital Rupee marketplace, where the CBDC can be utilised through the 
CBDC wallet. The marketplace has been connected, and many types of 
payments, like ticket booking, gift cards and all those things, can be made 
through CBDC as well. We have also launched our CBDC IVR services, whereby 
customers can utilise the CBDC offline also. 
- We have started our robotic process automation, wherein seven processes have 
been automated through RPA.  
- We have implemented a digital marketing solution so as to do digital marketing 
for our products. As we know, the bank has undertaken Project Parivartan, 
wherein our digital business balance sheet has grown to Rs.48,000 plus crore as 
on 30th September, 2026. To increase the digital business balance sheet size 
further, we have onboarded the digital marketing solution as well, which will 
help us in this. 
- We all know that UPI is also a very, very important payment channel, and 
constantly there are many, many improvements in the features of UPI. Recently, 
at the Global Fintech Forum in Mumbai, many new features were launched, and 
UCO Bank has also been participating in this. We have launched UPI Tap and 
Pay. We have launched UPI Help 2.0. And we have also launched a UPI 
automatic surveillance system, wherein any VPA or any QR code to which the 
customer wants to make a payment can be checked for its authenticity or 
genuineness. 
- In the same way, we have also launched an online self-service module, where 
customers can book certain services from the website of the bank.  
- We have also started a customer 360-degree portal in our branches, wherein the 
customer's entire 360-degree view is available to the branch. This helps branches 
to do cross-sell and provide better customer service. 

Page | 5  
 
- I already told you that we have opened a GIFT City branch in the last quarter, 
which has been doing good business as well. And we have launched many new 
products in Agri, Retail and MSME to take it ahead, as well as some products on 
the deposit side. We have done a launch for eFDR under MCX. We are already 
live for eFDR on BSE and NSE. Now we have added MCX also, the Multi 
Commodity Exchange, where brokers can make eFDR through our bank. 
- To strengthen our CASA position, we have done many MOUs with various 
government departments and large institutions. For example, we have entered 
into an MOU with the Government of Bihar for their employees' salary accounts. 
We have been empanelled by the state government of Rajasthan as well for the 
salary account package for their employees.  
- In the same way, in HR also, we have been doing recruitment wherever needed. 
In the current financial year we have recruited some specialist officers, which are 
data analysts, CAs, Trade Finance officers, etc., and for the next year also we 
have started some recruitment process for our professional officers and other 
customer service associates. 
- So, I think these are the major developments in the last quarter that we have 
undertaken to improve our service offering for the customers. And now, I open 
the floor for all the analysts and investors for their queries. We will try to reply to 
those queries.

- As far as SMA is concerned, you have said that, yes, there has been a little rise in

deposits will apply only on the new deposits. So that is the case there. But as of

on deposits. As of now we are maintaining whatever rate of interest is already 
there on the term deposits in our bank. Going forward, we will see the situation, 
how the requirement of deposits is, how the supply comes, and whether we need 
to increase it. We will take an appropriate call in due course of time.
